   note:  B renames `disposition` to `outcome` and keeps promoted/declined verbatim, but drops the `held — <what it waits on>` option; an undecided candidate in B simply has no outcome line yet, with no reason recorded (promoting-checked-candidates.md › promote).
unit-083 | narrowed | ## The candidates file
   quote: Status is derived from the last append and is the only field that changes.…
   note:  B keeps deriving status from the last line present (a candidate's status is never an authored/edited field, only read off the sequence of appends), but the `held` state and its "waits on something named" definition are gone — B's outcome step admits only promoted or declined.
unit-104 | narrowed | ## The corpus pair, and what is ordered
   quote: Every corpus in the buildout … is worked as an exploratory/verification pair, and the one hard ordering rule is exploratory pass on c → verification pass on c → any consumer of c…
   note:  B keeps "no evidence without a verification round" (candidates come only from a round, never a leads artifact) but drops the strict per-corpus exploratory-before-verification sequence — preparing-to-verify-a-corpus can be entered via building-a-tool or revising-the-method, or from an ad hoc question, with no exploration pass on that corpus required first; the unordered-exploratory-passes rule and "infrastructure runs when needed" aren't restated anywhere in B.
unit-160 | reversed | # The experiment lifecycle
   quote: One sequence, from a question to a promoted evidence entry, served by the agent runner's host at `/protocol` and kept in the repo as `fanout/PROTOCOL.md`. …
   note:  B retires fanout/PROTOCOL.md (as of 2026-09-05) and forbids treating it as the order's home; the order is instead derived from the v3-buildout process tables into map.md's generated graph, and the `/protocol` route is left to be rebuilt to serve that rendering ("a runner change still owed"), so the hand-kept order page the unit describes as current is no longer the mechanism.
unit-111 | absent | ## The four phases
   quote: Every WU of every type runs the same four phases in one HITL session (Fable): scope reconciliation, plan mode, execution, post-WU review…
   note:  B has no WU or fixed four-phase-in-one-session structure; work is a chain of separate activities (e.g. preparing-to-explore-a-corpus → exploring-a-corpus → reviewing-leads), each its own file, each process independently typed hitl/session/agent, not four fixed phases of one HITL session.
unit-112 | absent | ## The four phases
   quote: **1. Scope reconciliation** (auto mode)…
   note:  no forward plan, card, WU, or "auto mode" phase exists in B; the nearest artifact is the instance registry (SKILL.md › Instance registry), written once at Brian's go by a preparing activity's plan process, never reconciled afterward as a separate clerical step.
unit-113 | absent | ## The four phases
   quote: Exploratory | The card; the corpus's `CORPUS-STATUS.md` entry; the reading protocol; the arm design…
   note:  no "card" or hypothesis list exists per instance; preparing-to-explore-a-corpus § explore-plan reads question-list, corpus-status, corpus, state and skill and writes the plan fresh (scale, questions, arms) rather than reconciling pre-existing metadata, and the reading protocol/arm key are authored later in the same activity, not read beforehand.
unit-114 | narrowed | ## The four phases
   quote: Verification | The card; the corpus's spec pool; the named codebooks and their calibration records…
   note:  B keeps open questions (question-list) as the basis for scope and requires a calibrated codebook before a round, but there is no "card" or hypothesis list to recompute — a question names its hypotheses directly, and building/calibrating an uncalibrated codebook is its own separate process (author-codebook/calibrate), not something "flagged as the first task" of reconciliation.
unit-115 | absent | ## The four phases
   quote: Synthesis | The card; the debt status of every corpus it names…
   note:  B has no synthesis WU type or activity at all — no chain reads verified artifacts across corpora and writes synthesis findings gated on verification debt; the closest activities (exploring-a-corpus, reviewing-leads) operate on one corpus, not on the debt status of several.
unit-116 | narrowed | ## The four phases
   quote: Infrastructure | The card; the thing to build and what consumes it…
   note:  B keeps stating what is built and what consumes it, plus acceptance (tests, CORPUS-STATUS entry, Brian's checklist), but folds this into one single hitl build process rather than a phase-1-of-4 "scope reconciliation" step, and drops the "card"/WU framing entirely.
unit-117 | narrowed | ## The four phases
   quote: **2. Plan mode** (all types)…
   note:  B keeps "ask Brian's open questions batched four per call, then write the plan, then Brian approves" (explore-plan; also verify-plan, build) but each type's planning is its own activity file rather than a shared "phase 2"; synthesis as a type is dropped entirely, and "exit plan mode" as a named step doesn't exist.
unit-119 | narrowed | ## The four phases
   quote: Exploratory | Run the arms; bin disagreements if there is more than one…
   note:  B keeps running arms, binning disagreements and writing the leads artifact, but exploring-a-corpus only proposes questions (leads.md § Proposed questions) — writing them into the corpus's question list is a separate, Brian-led reviewing-leads step, not part of execution; there is no "card" to mark complete, since instance state is derived from artifacts.
unit-120 | narrowed | ## The four phases
   quote: Verification | Run the jobs; write the artifact; write the candidates file…
   note:  substance is kept (run jobs, write round.md, write candidates, run the referee, hold a promotion session, one commit, report counts) but split across four separately gated activities — conducting-a-verification-round, writing-candidates-from-verification, refereeing-a-candidate, promoting-checked-candidates — rather than one execution phase of a single WU session; `evidence-pipeline.md` no longer exists as a citation target.
unit-121 | absent | ## The four phases
   quote: Synthesis | Read the verified artifacts; write the synthesis artifact…
   note:  no synthesis activity exists in B; nothing reads verified artifacts across corpora, writes a synthesis artifact, or appends spec-pool questions for insights bearing on a hypothesis.
unit-122 | reversed | ## The four phases
   quote: Infrastructure | Build; test; calibrate if it is a codebook…
   note:  B keeps build/test/CORPUS-STATUS-update, but building-a-tool § Never explicitly forbids writing a question ("writes a candidate, a lead or a question"), where the old text has infrastructure execution append spec-pool questions if the build raised any; codebook calibration is also not part of building-a-tool at all — it is the separate hitl process preparing-to-verify-a-corpus § calibrate.
unit-123 | narrowed | ## The four phases
   quote: New-hypothesis proposals are held for the wrap-up in every type and offered only when novelty, testability and independence all hold.
   note:  the three criteria (novelty, testability, independence) and holding proposals for a later review/promotion session match closely for exploratory and verification, but "every type" no longer holds — building-a-tool (infrastructure) has no hypothesis-proposal wrap-up, and synthesis as a type is gone entirely.
unit-124 | narrowed | ## The four phases
   quote: **4. Post-WU review** with Brian, same session, two interleaving modes for all types, with one per-type difference in what "verify against the source" means:
   note:  B keeps Brian-led review that verifies findings against the source (reviewing-leads for exploratory; promoting-checked-candidates for verification), but these are separate, independently gated activities with their own preconditions, not "the same session" as execution or phase 4 of one WU; synthesis and infrastructure have no equivalent challenge/enrichment review structure.
unit-125 | narrowed | ## The four phases
   quote: *Challenge* — Brian questions a finding…
   note:  B keeps verifying a challenged finding against the source (the corpus itself, at the lead's locus) but never corrects the artifact in place — a lead only gets an appended, dated correction ("the lead itself is not edited"); synthesis as a type is gone entirely; the "corrected finding re-enters as a new candidate through the referee" detail isn't stated for a challenge (only reworded-hypothesis findings are re-queued, via iterating-a-statement).
unit-127 | narrowed | ## The four phases
   quote: Statement changes are batched at the end of the review, then handled as iterations (`evidence-pipeline.md` § Iteration)…
   note:  the story-content-drift redirect/out-of-scope language is kept almost verbatim (rule 7), but "batched at the end of the review" is dropped — iterating-a-statement is triggered by Brian's decision in a promotion session or any hitl session, not by batching at review's end, and reviewing-leads § Never explicitly forbids rewording a statement itself.
unit-084 | reversed | ## The referee
   quote: A **classifier in the verify role**, and therefore an instrument…
   note:  B's referee codebook is given only the target's current statement and the candidate's finding (artifacts.md § Codebook; refereeing-a-candidate.md § referee-materialise, § Never) — the cited source excerpt this unit says the runner hands the referee is exactly what B forbids giving it; calibration-before-first-batch survives, but re-hashing is superseded by explicit version numbering (codebook-N.md).
unit-086 | reversed | ## The referee
   quote: - **Inputs are exactly three**…
   note:  B gives the referee exactly two inputs — the target's current statement and the candidate's finding line — and explicitly withholds source, locator, excerpt and any other candidate (§ referee-materialise, § Never); the third input this unit requires (the cited source excerpt) is precisely what B's Never list forbids handing the referee.
unit-087 | narrowed | ## The referee
   quote: - **The task is to attempt the clause blind**…
   note:  The three classes and the mechanical tag survive, but B has the referee attempt the falsifier against the candidate's finding, never against a source excerpt (which it is never given, § referee-materialise) — less input than this unit describes the referee judging.
unit-089 | narrowed | ## The referee
   quote: - **A vacuous clause is non-diagnostic by definition, whoever wrote it**…
   note:  The vacuous-by-definition rule survives ("restates the claim instead of naming what the finding would have been… is non-diagnostic by definition"), but its object shifts from what the excerpt would contain to what the finding would have been, since the referee no longer sees an excerpt at all.
unit-161 | narrowed | ## The steps
   quote: | 1 | **Question** | HITL session | an entry in `docs/v3-framework/spec-pools/<corpus>.md` | …
   note:  same gate (a per-corpus question, HITL-written, under `questions/<corpus>.md` not `spec-pools/<corpus>.md`) but B exempts the referee instance, whose question is "the pipeline's own" with no question-list entry required.
unit-162 | absent | ## The steps
   quote: | 2 | **Cell and WU type** | HITL | the WU card: `Type`, `Corpus`, `Scale` (= the matrix cell) | …
   note:  B has no Type×Corpus×Scale matrix cell deciding model/context/verification; instances.md registers only id, type, corpus and go, and scale/arms/verification are fixed separately in explore-plan or verify-plan, while models are fixed per-process defaults in the activity tables.
unit-011 | absent | ## The work matrix
   quote: Every piece of buildout work sits in one cell of a 3 × 3 matrix…
   note:  B organizes work by activity and per-process mode/instruments/reads/writes (SKILL.md § Schema) instead of a 3×3 cell matrix; no cell vocabulary or grid remains.
unit-012 | narrowed | ## The work matrix
   quote: **item** — e.g. one note, passage, claim, candidate…
   note:  B keeps "item" and a frozen-predicate classifier judging one item, and keeps the story-content boundary (SKILL.md rules 1 and 7), but drops "investigator" as a distinct method-discretion item-role; verification is codebook classification only, not open per-claim evidence-finding.
unit-013 | narrowed | ## The work matrix
   quote: **slice** — e.g. one story, arc, analysis section…
   note:  B keeps "slice" and the slice reader, and keeps an auditor role (revising-the-method.md § audit-judge) at similar granularity, but drops "focused reader" entirely.
unit-014 | narrowed | ## The work matrix
   quote: **corpus** — everything, one context…
   note:  B keeps "corpus" and the pathfinder (one session reading the whole corpus), but drops "census" as a tool-based corpus-generate role.
unit-016 | absent | ## The work matrix
   quote: The cell names are the current set…
   note:  no cell/matrix concept exists to extend or misfit against; the closest mechanism, SKILL.md's router note that an unlisted activity is governed by its "closest row," works oppositely — it assigns the misfit rather than recording it unforced as a finding.
unit-017 | absent | ## The work matrix
   quote: Orthogonal to the cell: **role** — *generate* (produce records, labels, findings) or…
   note:  B never names a "role" axis; generate-type work (round-judge, calibrate-judge, referee-materialise) and verify-type work (referee-judge, audit-judge) exist but only as implicit properties of specific processes, never as a stated orthogonal generate/verify dimension.
unit-020 | narrowed | ## The work matrix
   quote: **Model, as revisable doctrine (2026-09-03), not a finding:** Fable for HITL design and…
   note:  B keeps per-process model defaults (Fable for pathfind; Opus for slice-read; Sonnet for round-judge, referee-judge, audit-judge) but drops "focused reader" and "investigator" entirely and states no doctrine that model-comparison experiments must hold model constant or that the allocation is a default rather than a task rule.
unit-021 | narrowed | ## The work matrix
   quote: **Verification owed.** The more discretion, the more checking downstream…
   note:  B keeps calibration as what makes a codebook/classifier trusted (rule 4) and keeps "leads only, never a finding" for exploration, but generalizes leads-only to every exploration output including slice readers (rule 2; artifacts.md › Leads artifact), removing the slice reader's separate path to elevated trust via a second blind reader.
unit-150 | absent | ## Trigger and scope
   quote: On Brian's demand …
   note:  No activity in B triggers a whole-set review of the hypothesis set on Brian's judgment (tangled, duplicates, too many challenged); minting-a-hypothesis and iterating-a-statement handle individual merges/splits but re-mint/re-word only the affected files, and neither instructs re-pointing a question-list's `hypotheses` line after a merge or split, nor names "spec pool", the index, or a forward plan as scope for such a pass.
unit-003 | narrowed | # V3 framework buildout — revision 1
   quote: Why revision 1 exists, and what it replaced, is recorded once in…
   note:  B states the same provenance-vs-instruction pattern ("this skill is the instruction") but only spells it out for revision 2's own note (`methodology-revision-2.md`); revision 1's note is referenced only implicitly via the generic `methodology-revision-N.md` naming and the parenthetical "(revision 1, 2026-09-03)", not restated as its own claim.
unit-094 | narrowed | ## Verification debt and codebook versioning
   quote: A corpus's exploratory pass opens a debt paid only by its verification pass. …
   note:  B keeps leads-not-evidence-until-verified (rule 3) and free flow of questions between corpora (rule 3; question-list format), but a verification pass alone no longer pays the debt — rule 2 requires the finding also pass a fresh-context referee and Brian's promotion decision before it becomes evidence; "spec pool" is now the per-corpus question-list.
unit-095 | narrowed | ## Verification debt and codebook versioning
   quote: Every verification result cites the codebook hash it was produced under. …
   note:  B keeps "every result cites the hash" and "a revision is a new version and a re-run, never a re-label" (rule 4), but does not carry the requirement that old results be marked superseded (results are simply frozen, and a superseded codebook version just stays on disk), and does not restate the affordability rationale that re-runs are cheap because the work is classifier-tier.
unit-151 | narrowed | ## What it does
   quote: Merges (one claim in two wordings)…
   note:  B's merge/split ceremony covers only merges and splits; emergent-cluster formation and orphan-handling as restructuring types have no counterpart anywhere in B.
unit-153 | narrowed | ## What it does
   quote: Structural changes follow `hypothesis-records.md` § Ceremony scaling…
   note:  B keeps new files, an iteration entry in each old file naming its replacement, and ids never reused, but drops the mandated "old status challenged" — status is instead computed from current-wording entries, which after supersession are none.
unit-154 | absent | ## What it does
   quote: Re-points spec-pool entries and forward-plan references to the surviving ids.
   note:  B has no spec-pool or forward-plan artifacts to re-point; merge/split re-pointing in B is limited to queuing prior findings as iteration candidates for the referee.
unit-157 | absent | ## What it produces
   quote: `docs/v3-framework/consolidation-N.md` — write-once, the set-level provenance: what merged, split, was archived or created, why, and what the landscape looks like now. …
   note:  B records merge/split provenance only per-file (an iteration entry on each superseded file, a `created` entry naming the files a merge or split came from); no write-once artifact holds the set-level story of what merged, split, was archived or created and why.
unit-159 | reversed | ## What it produces
   quote: A pending forward plan: consolidation always requires a new plan, because the old plan's references are stale. …
   note:  B abolishes the forward plan entirely ("There is no plan: what to do next is read from the generated `state.md`, and the pick is Brian's"; revision 1's forward plans are kept only as retired reference), so no activity, consolidation included, ever requires producing a new plan.
unit-060 | narrowed | ## What never enters a record
   quote: Observations that do not change the statement (a spec-pool question, or nothing).
   note:  B keeps "observations that do not change the statement" as excluded, but drops the parenthetical naming its two possible dispositions (a question, or nothing).
unit-061 | narrowed | ## What never enters a record
   quote: Methodological pointers ("WU2.4 should check this" — the forward plan or spec pool).
   note:  B keeps "pointers to future work" as excluded and names only the question list as their destination; the "forward plan" destination has no counterpart (SKILL.md lists forward plans among revision 1's retired, reference-only artifacts).
unit-045 | narrowed | ## What this skill does not govern
   quote: Among other things: story content decisions; prose technique (the planner specifies goals and mechanisms, never how to write); planner features…
   note:  B keeps the four items and the hypothesis/baselining closer, but drops "Among other things" (the list's non-exhaustive framing), the parenthetical explaining prose technique ("the planner specifies goals and mechanisms, never how to write"), and the explicit instruction to check FEATURE-AUDIT before proposing anything touching the feature set.
unit-073 | narrowed | ## Where each kind of write goes
   quote: A finding of an exploratory pass …
   note:  B calls this the leads-artifact (docs/v3-framework/<instance>/leads.md) and requires it hold leads only — never a finding or a claim about a hypothesis.
unit-074 | narrowed | ## Where each kind of write goes
   quote: A question raised about a corpus …
   note:  B keeps questions/<corpus>.md as the destination but restricts writing to hitl processes only — never "any pass" or a post-review by itself.
unit-075 | narrowed | ## Where each kind of write goes
   quote: A candidate (a finding that a verification pass claims bears on a hypothesis) …
   note:  B keeps fanout/<instance>/candidates.md as the destination but assigns the write to a separate writing-candidates-from-verification session reading the round's tally, not to the verification pass itself.
unit-147 | reversed | ## Writing the plan
   quote: Start from the landscape: read the full index and every hypothesis file …
   note:  B states "there is no plan: what to do next is read from the generated state.md, and the pick is Brian's" — the landscape-survey document this unit describes is eliminated; per-instance verify-plan/explore-plan (preparing-to-verify-a-corpus.md, preparing-to-explore-a-corpus.md) ask narrower, single-instance planning questions rather than surveying every hypothesis and grouping by corpus, and "spec pool" is not a concept in B (its nearest analogue, the corpus question-list, is checked per-instance, not landscape-wide); "consolidation report" and "evidence-pipeline.md" have no counterpart in B.
unit-148 | absent | ## Writing the plan
   quote: The rationale section is written once and can be long — at least: what the last consolidation, revision or reassessment showed …
   note:  B has no "the plan" document, no rationale section of that kind, and no "cards" sized for a plan-mode session to scope execution; the nearest artifact in shape, revising-the-method's write-once revision-note, is a different document serving methodology revisions only, not landscape-wide hypothesis planning, so it does not carry this instruction.
unit-128 | narrowed | ## WU artifacts
   quote: `docs/v3-framework/WU<plan>.<unit>-<slug>.md` or a directory of that name when the WU has several files (records, renders, manifests)…
   note:  B drops the WU<plan>.<unit>-<slug> naming and single-folder scheme entirely, replacing it with per-instance folders (registry id) under docs/v3-framework/ and fanout/; jobs, items, results, ledger and candidates are still colocated under fanout/<instance>/<run>/ and fanout/<instance>/candidates.md, but no single artifact now carries the full "whatever it takes to re-run" method statement — it is split across run.md, round.md/leads.md, each with its own mutation rule instead of one blanket write-once rule.
